main_text.p: rum virtute imbutus, quo fit ut coagulet hydrargyrum:
Alias illo destitutum destruit metalla, non perficit,
Sal ex eo album fixum est, & albam tinctu-ram conferre potest.

ArsenicumArsenicum est succus mineralis, pin-guis, inflammatilis, vicino[?] sulphuri, viru-lentior tamen, ob salem conjunctum, constans pinguedine sulphurea, hydrar-gyro pauco, & spiritu salis albi, quorum pars volatica est, pars fixioni propior.

Chalcan-thumChalcanthum est succus metallicus naturae aerosae, constans ex terra aerosa, alumine & sulphure, & ob id etiam acorem habet virosum & stipticum cum dulcedine conjunctum, resolvituráque in terram citrinam, succum aluminosum, & pinguedinem sulphuream.
Destillatur ex eo acidus liquor, & o-leum rubeum, ex quo spiritus pinguis colligitur.
Atrum colorem gignit in succis plan-tarum, unde atramentum sutorium di-ctum.

page.notes: The page number "188" is printed in the top left corner and is read as 188. The word "vicino" has a superscript mark that may be a flourish or a letter, so it is marked [?]. The marginal notes carry no reference marks in the text. The catchword "Trans-" is printed at the lower right. Some letters in the main text are small and worn, but the readings are clear.
